findings.claim: The commit message states that 32 chains were newly registered, but the safe-deployments 1.37.62 upgrade only adds 1.5.0 support for 13 chains (10, 146, 196, 232, 324, 3338, 5000, 42161, 43114, 57073, 59144, 80094, 1313161554), so the commit/PR description does not match the actual change.
This package.json also bumps to the same safe-deployments version that only covers 13 chains rather than the 32 described, so it shares the same description/scope mismatch.

If the referenced WA-2918 ticket lists 32 chains, then 1.5.0 Safes on the roughly 19 chains not covered by this bump will continue to receive 'not compatible' or untrusted-handler results after the merge.

A newer version, 1.37.63, is already published and adds 1.5.0 support for additional chains (1328, 2818, 6498, 314159, 936485), suggesting the dependency should potentially be bumped to ^1.37.63 instead of 1.37.62, or the discrepancy should be reconciled before merging.

packages/utils imports @safe-global/safe-deployments directly in its source but does not list it as a dependency in package.json, relying on Yarn's deduplication to get the correct version, which is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this change.

apps/mobile also imports @safe-global/safe-deployments directly without declaring it as a dependency, so if Yarn's single merged lockfile entry for the package ever splits, mobile and utils could silently end up running different deployment data than the web app.

No test covers 1.5.0 support on any of the newly added chains, even though this is the main user-facing effect of the version bump; the existing test file already references chains 10 and 324, which both gained 1.5.0 support in this release, but no assertions were added for them.
